pr_title: fix: boundary predicate to block all accumulated predicates in push down
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12102.

This adjusts some earlier fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/5951 and https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/5951 to remove handling of `predicate_is_pushdown_boundary` from `Distinct` and `MapFunction::Explode`. Instead, all boundary predicates are handled in `Selection` and are not expected to leak outside of `Selection`.

Also, very strangely, the formatter isn't working properly inside the `match` block in `push_down` (would be cool if anyone knows why).
pr_comments:
@ritchie46 , will need to remove `transfer_to_local_by_nodes` from `partition_by_full_context` as well, I'll push a commit for it:

```python
lf = (
    pl.scan_parquet("py-polars/tests/unit/io/files/foods1.parquet")
    .filter(pl.col("category") == pl.col("category").take(0))
    .filter(pl.col("sugars_g") != 2)  # first row sugars_g == 2
)

print(lf.explain())
# FILTER [(col("category")) == (col("category").take(0))] FROM  <--- boundary here

#   Parquet SCAN py-polars/tests/unit/io/files/foods1.parquet
#   PROJECT */4 COLUMNS
#   SELECTION: [(col("sugars_g")) != (2)]  <--- pushed past boundary
print(lf.explain(predicate_pushdown=False))
# FILTER [(col("sugars_g")) != (2)] FROM
# FILTER [(col("category")) == (col("category").take(0))] FROM

#   Parquet SCAN py-polars/tests/unit/io/files/foods1.parquet
#   PROJECT */4 COLUMNS
```

*note that the above snippet is only possible because of https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12116 - where `match::Selection` is allowing `.take()` to be pushed down, since otherwise `.take()` would be blocked at `match::Selection` and never hit `match::Scan`.

issue_context.title: Incorrect predicate pushdown across pushdown boundary
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame(dict(x=[1, 2, 4]))

lf = (
    df.lazy()
    .filter(pl.col("x") > 1)
    .filter(pl.col("x") >= 2)
    .filter(pl.col("x") == pl.min("x"))
    .filter(pl.col("x") > 3)
)

print(lf.explain())
# FILTER [(col("x")) == (col("x").min())] FROM  <--- pushdown boundary here
# DF ["x"]; PROJECT */1 COLUMNS; SELECTION: "[([(col(\"x\")) > (1)]) & ([([(col(\"x\")) >= (2)]) & ([(col(\"x\")) > (3)])])]"
#                                                                                                  ^^^
#                                                                                 incorrectly pushed across pushdown boundary
print(lf.collect())
# >>> print(lf.collect())  # gives incorrect result
# shape: (1, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ x   │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 4   │
# └─────┘
print(lf.explain(optimized=False))
# FILTER [(col("x")) > (3)] FROM
# FILTER [(col("x")) == (col("x").min())] FROM
# FILTER [(col("x")) >= (2)] FROM
# FILTER [(col("x")) > (1)] FROM
# DF ["x"]; PROJECT */1 COLUMNS; SELECTION: "None"
print(lf.collect(no_optimization=True))  # gives correct result
# shape: (0, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ x   │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# └─────┘

```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

The predicate pushdown optimizer blocks pushdown of boundary predicates, however subsequent predicates are still incorrectly pushed past the boundary.

At https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/6bc3896216b05ffcff54f6902148d79c36ca08cd/crates/polars-plan/src/logical_plan/optimizer/predicate_pushdown/mod.rs#L197, observe that boundary predicates are transferred to local predicates, but predicates subsequent to the boundary predicate are not considered.

### Expected behavior

Predicates not to be pushed past boundary predicates during optimization.

review_comments: I'm speculating that it may be possible for all groups-sensitive predicates to be moved to local by `push_down::match::Selection`, making it so that there are never any groups-sensitive predicates at this point

So what will happen if we don't have `Selection`, for example, the predicate is pushed down from `Join`? I didn't look at all the changes carefully, but I was a little curious when I saw this comment.

Yeah, in that case there will still be groups-sensitive predicates. But from what I've observed, I think for a predicate to be in `Join`, it must have been pushed into that `Join` during/after optimization from a `Selection` that existed after it (?). It doesn't seem to be possible to directly create a `Join` node containing a predicate from any user API (although definitely possible by directly importing from `polars_plan` in rust). For example, in py-polars you would have to do `.join(...).filter(...)`, which creates the `Selection`.

So I think the requirement behind being able to handle all boundary/groups-sensitive predicates in `push_down::match::Selection` is for all predicates to originate from `Selection` nodes (before optimization, and this could be checked as well). Then, because `Selection` can guarantee to block if there are boundary predicates, all other nodes would not need to check for boundaries, they would only need to check for `Node`-specific blocking rules (e.g. explode would only need to take out predicates dependent on the exploded column names).

If on the other hand there can be predicates in non-`Selection` nodes at the start of predicate push down, then I imagine that all of those nodes that have predicates would need to do the check for boundary predicates and block appropriately. Or maybe the predicates can first be moved out to `Selection` nodes first before starting push down.
Predicates should only ever be pushed down from `filters`, e.g. `Selection` nodes.

Doesn't swapping resolve it. E.g. wouldn't keeping `transfer_to_local_by_node` here work?

As it is we are now removing all predicates even orthogonal ones.

I think they need to all be removed - orthogonal predicates would still affect the inputs to e.g. aggregation expressions (even though the predicates themselves may not be affected). The comment in the code could definitely be improved though.
